package com.fitt.identity.controller;

import com.fitt.identity.dto.LoginRequest;
import com.fitt.identity.dto.RegisterRequest;
import com.fitt.identity.dto.TokenResponse;
import com.fitt.identity.service.IdentityAuthService;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

// Thin controller, HTTP concerns only.
// Parses the request, calls the service, returns the response.
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/identity/auth")
public class IdentityAuthController {

    private final IdentityAuthService identityAuthService;

    public IdentityAuthController(IdentityAuthService identityAuthService) {
        this.identityAuthService = identityAuthService;
    }

    // Returns 201 so the client knows a resource was created.
    // Token is included so the user is logged in immediately after sign up.
    @PostMapping("/register")
    public ResponseEntity<TokenResponse> register(@RequestBody RegisterRequest request) {
        String token = identityAuthService.register(request.getEmail(), request.getPassword());
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CREATED).body(new TokenResponse(token));
    }

    // Public endpoint, configured in SecurityConfig.
    // 401 is handled automatically by Spring Security if credentials fail.
    @PostMapping("/login")
    public ResponseEntity<TokenResponse> login(@RequestBody LoginRequest request) {
        String token = identityAuthService.login(request.getEmail(), request.getPassword());
        return ResponseEntity.ok(new TokenResponse(token));
    }
}

@RestController

    private final IdentityHealthService identityHealthService;

package com.fitt.identity.domain;

import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;
import org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority;
import org.springframework.security.core.authority.SimpleGrantedAuthority;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetails;

import java.util.Collection;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "users")
public class UserEntity implements UserDetails {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @Column(nullable = false, unique = true)
    private String email;

    // Explicitly mapped so Hibernate does not guess the column name.
    @Column(name = "password_hash", nullable = false)
    private String passwordHash;

    // JPA needs this to rebuild objects from query results.
    // Protected so nothing in application code calls it directly.
    protected UserEntity() {}

    public UserEntity(String email, String passwordHash) {
        this.email = email;
        this.passwordHash = passwordHash;
    }

    public Long getId() {
        return id;
    }

    // Email is the login identifier for FITT so this returns email.
    @Override
    public String getUsername() {
        return email;
    }

    // Returns the BCrypt hash stored in DB.
    // DaoAuthenticationProvider calls matches(rawPassword, getPassword()) at login time.
    @Override
    public String getPassword() {
        return passwordHash;
    }

    // No role system in v1 but Spring Security needs at least one authority.
    @Override
    public Collection<? extends GrantedAuthority> getAuthorities() {
        return List.of(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_USER"));
    }

    // No account locking or expiration in v1.
    @Override
    public boolean isAccountNonExpired() { return true; }

    @Override
    public boolean isAccountNonLocked() { return true; }

    @Override
    public boolean isCredentialsNonExpired() { return true; }

    @Override
    public boolean isEnabled() { return true; }
}

import java.time.Instant;

public class IdentityHealthResponse {

    private final String status;
    private final Instant timestamp;
    private final String provider;

    public IdentityHealthResponse(String status, Instant timestamp, String provider) {
        this.status = status;
        this.timestamp = timestamp;
        this.provider = provider;
    }

    public String getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    public Instant getTimestamp() {
        return timestamp;
    }

    public String getProvider() {
        return provider;
    }
}

package com.fitt.identity.dto;

// What gets sent back to the client after a successful login.
// The client stores this and attaches it to every future request as:
// Authorization: Bearer <token>
public class TokenResponse {

    private final String token;

    public TokenResponse(String token) {
        this.token = token;
    }

    public String getToken() {
        return token;
    }
}

package com.fitt.identity.repository;

import com.fitt.identity.domain.UserEntity;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;

import java.util.Optional;

public interface UserRepository extends JpaRepository<UserEntity, Long> {

    Optional<UserEntity> findByEmail(String email);

    // Used in registration to check for duplicates before hitting the DB with a save.
    boolean existsByEmail(String email);
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/identity/service/IdentityAuthService.java

package com.fitt.identity.service;

import com.fitt.identity.domain.UserEntity;
import com.fitt.identity.repository.UserRepository;
import com.fitt.identity.service.exception.EmailAlreadyExistsException;
import com.fitt.shared.properties.JwtProperties;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationManager;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken;
import org.springframework.security.core.Authentication;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jose.jws.MacAlgorithm;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwsHeader;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwtClaimsSet;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwtEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwtEncoderParameters;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.time.Instant;

@Service
public class IdentityAuthService {

    private final AuthenticationManager authenticationManager;
    private final JwtEncoder jwtEncoder;
    private final JwtProperties jwtProperties;
    private final UserRepository userRepository;
    private final PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder;

    public IdentityAuthService(
            AuthenticationManager authenticationManager,
            JwtEncoder jwtEncoder,
            JwtProperties jwtProperties,
            UserRepository userRepository,
            PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder
    ) {
        this.authenticationManager = authenticationManager;
        this.jwtEncoder = jwtEncoder;
        this.jwtProperties = jwtProperties;
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
        this.passwordEncoder = passwordEncoder;
    }

    // Duplicate check runs first so we return a clean 409 instead of letting
    // a DB constraint violation bubble up as a 500.
    // Password is hashed before the entity is built so plain text never hits the DB.
    public String register(String email, String password) {
        if (userRepository.existsByEmail(email)) {
            throw new EmailAlreadyExistsException("email already registered");
        }

        String hash = passwordEncoder.encode(password);
        UserEntity saved = userRepository.save(new UserEntity(email, hash));

        return buildToken(saved);
    }

    // AuthenticationManager runs the full verification chain.
    // Wrong credentials throw AuthenticationException and Spring Security returns 401.
    // Pattern matching instanceof checks the type and binds in one step.
    // In practice this never fails because loadUserByUsername always returns a UserEntity,
    // but failing fast here is cleaner than letting a ClassCastException surface later.
    public String login(String email, String password) {
        Authentication auth = authenticationManager.authenticate(
                new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(email, password)
        );

        Object principal = auth.getPrincipal();
        if (!(principal instanceof UserEntity user)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("unexpected principal type after authentication");
        }

        return buildToken(user);
    }

    // Shared by register and login so token structure has one place to change.
    private String buildToken(UserEntity user) {
        Instant now = Instant.now();

        JwtClaimsSet claims = JwtClaimsSet.builder()
                .issuer(jwtProperties.getIssuer())
                .subject(user.getUsername())
                .issuedAt(now)
                .expiresAt(now.plusSeconds(jwtProperties.getTtlSeconds()))
                .claim("uid", user.getId())
                .build();

        JwsHeader header = JwsHeader.with(MacAlgorithm.HS256).build();
        return jwtEncoder.encode(JwtEncoderParameters.from(header, claims)).getTokenValue();
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/identity/service/IdentityUserDetailsService.java

package com.fitt.identity.service;

import com.fitt.identity.repository.UserRepository;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetails;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetailsService;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UsernameNotFoundException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class IdentityUserDetailsService implements UserDetailsService {

    private final UserRepository userRepository;

    public IdentityUserDetailsService(UserRepository userRepository) {
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
    }

    // DaoAuthenticationProvider calls this on every login attempt.
    // The interface says "username" but for FITT this is always the email.
    // Keeping the error vague so callers cannot tell if an email exists.
    @Override
    public UserDetails loadUserByUsername(String email) throws UsernameNotFoundException {
        return userRepository.findByEmail(email)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new UsernameNotFoundException("bad credentials"));
    }
}

package com.fitt.shared.config;

import com.fitt.identity.service.exception.EmailAlreadyExistsException;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.ExerciseNotFoundException;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.WorkoutPlanNotFoundException;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.WorkoutSessionNotFoundException;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.BadCredentialsException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestControllerAdvice;

@RestControllerAdvice
public class ApiExceptionHandler {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ApiExceptionHandler.class);

    // workouts domain, 404s
    @ExceptionHandler(WorkoutSessionNotFoundException.class)
    public ProblemDetail handleWorkoutSessionNotFound(WorkoutSessionNotFoundException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ex.getMessage());
        problem.setTitle("Workout Session Not Found");
        return problem;
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(WorkoutPlanNotFoundException.class)
    public ProblemDetail handleWorkoutPlanNotFound(WorkoutPlanNotFoundException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ex.getMessage());
        problem.setTitle("Workout Plan Not Found");
        return problem;
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(ExerciseNotFoundException.class)
    public ProblemDetail handleExerciseNotFound(ExerciseNotFoundException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ex.getMessage());
        problem.setTitle("Exercise Not Found");
        return problem;
    }

    // bad requests from the workouts domain (fixed exercise delete, bad entry IDs, etc)
    @ExceptionHandler(IllegalArgumentException.class)
    public ProblemDetail handleIllegalArgument(IllegalArgumentException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, ex.getMessage());
        problem.setTitle("Bad Request");
        return problem;
    }

    // 409 because the request is valid but conflicts with existing data.
    @ExceptionHandler(EmailAlreadyExistsException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleEmailAlreadyExists(EmailAlreadyExistsException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
        problem.setTitle("Conflict");
        problem.setDetail(ex.getMessage());
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CONFLICT).body(problem);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(IllegalArgumentException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleBadRequest(IllegalArgumentException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
        problem.setTitle("Bad Request");
        problem.setDetail(ex.getMessage());
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST).body(problem);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleUnexpected(Exception ex) {
        log.error("Unhandled exception", ex);

        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR);
        problem.setTitle("Internal Server Error");
        problem.setDetail("Unexpected error");
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR).body(problem);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(BadCredentialsException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleBadCredential(BadCredentialsException ex) {
        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED);
        problem.setTitle("Bad Credentials");
        problem.setDetail(ex.getMessage());
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED).body(problem);
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/shared/config/JwtBeansConfig.java
================================================================================
package com.fitt.shared.config;

import com.fitt.shared.properties.JwtProperties;
import com.nimbusds.jose.jwk.JWKSet;
import com.nimbusds.jose.jwk.OctetSequenceKey;
import com.nimbusds.jose.jwk.source.ImmutableJWKSet;
import com.nimbusds.jose.proc.SecurityContext;
import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.EnableConfigurationProperties;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwtDecoder;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.JwtEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.NimbusJwtDecoder;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.NimbusJwtEncoder;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import javax.crypto.SecretKey;
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

// All JWT infrastructure lives here: secret key, decoder, and encoder.
// @EnableConfigurationProperties is what actually activates JwtProperties binding.
// Without it the fields stay null and nothing works.
@Configuration
@EnableConfigurationProperties(JwtProperties.class)
public class JwtBeansConfig {

    // Converts the plain string secret into a real cryptographic key.
    // SecretKeySpec wraps raw bytes into something the JCA (Java Cryptography Architecture)
    // understands. Failing fast here is intentional. Better than a silent misconfiguration
    // that only shows up at runtime.
    @Bean
    public SecretKey jwtSecretKey(JwtProperties props) {
        byte[] keyBytes = props.getSecretValue().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        if (keyBytes.length < 32) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "fitt.jwt.secret-value must be at least 32 characters (256 bits) for HS256"
            );
        }
        return new SecretKeySpec(keyBytes, "HmacSHA256");
    }

    // The decoder is used automatically by Spring Security's BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter.
    // On every protected request it checks the signature, verifies expiration, and extracts
    // the claims. Never called manually, the filter chain handles it.
    @Bean
    public JwtDecoder jwtDecoder(SecretKey jwtSecretKey) {
        return NimbusJwtDecoder.withSecretKey(jwtSecretKey).build();
    }

    // The encoder gets called explicitly at login to create and sign a new token.
    // Nimbus requires the key in JWK (JSON Web Key) format. OctetSequenceKey is the
    // correct JWK type for symmetric keys like this one.
    @Bean
    public JwtEncoder jwtEncoder(SecretKey jwtSecretKey) {
        OctetSequenceKey jwk = new OctetSequenceKey.Builder(jwtSecretKey.getEncoded())
                .algorithm(com.nimbusds.jose.JWSAlgorithm.HS256)
                .keyID("fitt-key-1")   // Nimbus requires a key ID to select the right key from the set
                .build();
        ImmutableJWKSet<SecurityContext> jwkSet = new ImmutableJWKSet<>(new JWKSet(jwk));
        return new NimbusJwtEncoder(jwkSet);
    }

    // Spring Boot 4 / Jackson 3 auto configures ObjectMapper, but the security handlers
    // inject JsonMapper by type specifically. Declaring it here lets Spring resolve that
    // dependency. JsonMapper is the concrete JSON only subclass of ObjectMapper.
    @Bean
    public JsonMapper jsonMapper() {
        return JsonMapper.builder().build();
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/shared/config/SecurityConfig.java
================================================================================
package com.fitt.shared.config;

import com.fitt.identity.service.IdentityUserDetailsService;
import com.fitt.shared.security.RestAccessDeniedHandler;
import com.fitt.shared.security.RestAuthenticationEntryPoint;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationManager;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.ProviderManager;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.dao.DaoAuthenticationProvider;
import org.springframework.security.config.Customizer;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configurers.AbstractHttpConfigurer;
import org.springframework.security.config.http.SessionCreationPolicy;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;
import org.springframework.web.cors.CorsConfiguration;
import org.springframework.web.cors.CorsConfigurationSource;
import org.springframework.web.cors.UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource;

import java.util.List;

@Configuration
public class SecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    public SecurityFilterChain securityFilterChain(
            HttpSecurity http,
            RestAuthenticationEntryPoint authenticationEntryPoint,
            RestAccessDeniedHandler accessDeniedHandler
    ) throws Exception {

        return http
                .csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)

                // Configured here rather than at the MVC layer because Spring Security
                // filters run before the DispatcherServlet. A preflight OPTIONS request
                // would be rejected with 401 before MVC ever sees it without this.
                .cors(cors -> cors.configurationSource(corsConfigurationSource()))

                .sessionManagement(session -> session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))

                .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                        .requestMatchers("/api/health").permitAll()
                        .requestMatchers("/api/identity/health").permitAll()
                        .requestMatchers("/api/identity/auth/login").permitAll()
                        .requestMatchers("/api/identity/auth/register").permitAll()
                        .anyRequest().authenticated()
                )

                .oauth2ResourceServer(oauth2 -> oauth2.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()))

                .exceptionHandling(ex -> ex
                        .authenticationEntryPoint(authenticationEntryPoint)
                        .accessDeniedHandler(accessDeniedHandler)
                )

                .build();
    }

    // X-Request-ID is listed so the correlation ID header passes the preflight check.
    // allowCredentials(true) requires a named origin, wildcard is not allowed with credentials.
    @Bean
    public CorsConfigurationSource corsConfigurationSource() {
        CorsConfiguration config = new CorsConfiguration();
        config.setAllowedOrigins(List.of("http://localhost:4200"));
        config.setAllowedMethods(List.of("GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"));
        config.setAllowedHeaders(List.of("Authorization", "Content-Type", "X-Request-ID"));
        config.setExposedHeaders(List.of("X-Request-ID"));
        config.setAllowCredentials(true);
        config.setMaxAge(3600L);

        UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource source = new UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource();
        source.registerCorsConfiguration("/**", config);
        return source;
    }

    // Explicit wiring so it is clear exactly which service and encoder are used.
    // Nothing is auto-detected here.
    @Bean
    public DaoAuthenticationProvider authenticationProvider(
            IdentityUserDetailsService userDetailsService,
            PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder
    ) {
        DaoAuthenticationProvider provider = new DaoAuthenticationProvider(userDetailsService);
        provider.setPasswordEncoder(passwordEncoder);
        return provider;
    }

    // ProviderManager is the standard AuthenticationManager implementation.
    // Exposed as a bean so IdentityAuthService can inject and call it directly.
    @Bean
    public AuthenticationManager authenticationManager(DaoAuthenticationProvider authenticationProvider) {
        return new ProviderManager(authenticationProvider);
    }

    @Bean
    public PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
        return new BCryptPasswordEncoder();
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/shared/filter/CorrelationIdFilter.java
================================================================================
package com.fitt.shared.filter;

import jakarta.servlet.FilterChain;
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import org.slf4j.MDC;
import org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.UUID;

// Stores the incoming X-Request-ID in the MDC so every log line produced
// during this request automatically includes the correlation ID.
// The ID is echoed in the response so callers can match client and server logs.
@Component
public class CorrelationIdFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {

    private static final String REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID";
    private static final String MDC_KEY = "requestId";

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(
            @NonNull HttpServletRequest request,
            @NonNull HttpServletResponse response,
            @NonNull FilterChain filterChain
    ) throws ServletException, IOException {

        String requestId = request.getHeader(REQUEST_ID_HEADER);

        if (requestId == null || requestId.isBlank()) {
            requestId = UUID.randomUUID().toString();
        }

        MDC.put(MDC_KEY, requestId);
        response.setHeader(REQUEST_ID_HEADER, requestId);

        try {
            filterChain.doFilter(request, response);
        } finally {
            // Tomcat reuses threads from a pool. Without clearing here, this
            // requests correlation ID would appear in the next requests log lines.
            MDC.clear();
        }
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/shared/properties/JwtProperties.java

package com.fitt.shared.properties;

import org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties;

// Instead of scattering @Value annotations everywhere, @ConfigurationProperties
// binds all "fitt.jwt.*" properties into one typed class. Much cleaner approach.
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "fitt.jwt")
public class JwtProperties {

    // The secret used to sign and verify tokens. Has to be at least 32 chars (256 bits)
    // for HS256. Enforced in JwtBeansConfig so it fails fast if misconfigured.
    // Never put a real production value here. Use environment-specific properties files.
    private String secretValue;

    // Gets embedded into every token as the "iss" claim.
    // The decoder checks incoming tokens against this, so both sides need to agree on the value.
    private String issuer = "fitt-api";

    // How long a token stays valid, in seconds. 1 hour by default.
    // Shorter lived tokens limit the damage if one gets stolen.
    private long ttlSeconds = 3600;

    public String getSecretValue() {
        return secretValue;
    }

    public void setSecretValue(String secretValue) {
        this.secretValue = secretValue;
    }

    public String getIssuer() {
        return issuer;
    }

    public void setIssuer(String issuer) {
        this.issuer = issuer;
    }

    public long getTtlSeconds() {
        return ttlSeconds;
    }

    public void setTtlSeconds(long ttlSeconds) {
        this.ttlSeconds = ttlSeconds;
    }
}

package com.fitt.shared.security;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.security.web.access.AccessDeniedHandler;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.io.IOException;

@Component
public class RestAccessDeniedHandler implements AccessDeniedHandler {

    private final JsonMapper jsonMapper;

    public RestAccessDeniedHandler(JsonMapper jsonMapper) {
        this.jsonMapper = jsonMapper;
    }

    @Override
    public void handle(
            HttpServletRequest request,
            HttpServletResponse response,
            AccessDeniedException accessDeniedException
    ) throws IOException {

        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
        problem.setTitle("Forbidden");
        problem.setDetail("You do not have access to this resource");

        response.setStatus(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN.value());
        response.setContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE);

        jsonMapper.writeValue(response.getOutputStream(), problem);
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/shared/security/RestAuthenticationEntryPoint.java

package com.fitt.shared.security;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import org.springframework.http.HttpHeaders;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.security.core.AuthenticationException;
import org.springframework.security.web.AuthenticationEntryPoint;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.io.IOException;

@Component
public class RestAuthenticationEntryPoint implements AuthenticationEntryPoint {

    private final JsonMapper jsonMapper;

    public RestAuthenticationEntryPoint(JsonMapper jsonMapper) {
        this.jsonMapper = jsonMapper;
    }

    @Override
    public void commence(
            HttpServletRequest request,
            HttpServletResponse response,
            AuthenticationException authException
    ) throws IOException {

        ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatus(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED);
        problem.setTitle("Unauthorized");
        problem.setDetail("Authentication is required");

        response.setStatus(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED.value());
        response.setHeader(HttpHeaders.WWW_AUTHENTICATE, "Bearer");
        response.setContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE);

        jsonMapper.writeValue(response.getOutputStream(), problem);
    }
}

package com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

@Entity
@Table(name = "exercises")
public class ExerciseEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Null means global exercise available to all users.
    // Non-null means user-created custom exercise.
    @Column(name = "owner_user_id")
    private Long ownerUserId;

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String name;

    @Column(name = "muscle_group", nullable = false)
    private String muscleGroup;

    // Convenience flag, mirrors whether ownerUserId is null.
    // Avoids null checks in query logic.
    @Column(name = "is_custom", nullable = false)
    private boolean isCustom;

    protected ExerciseEntity() {}

    public ExerciseEntity(Long ownerUserId, String name, String muscleGroup, boolean isCustom) {
        this.ownerUserId = ownerUserId;
        this.name = name;
        this.muscleGroup = muscleGroup;
        this.isCustom = isCustom;
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public Long getOwnerUserId() { return ownerUserId; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public String getMuscleGroup() { return muscleGroup; }
    public boolean isCustom() { return isCustom; }

    public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; }
    public void setMuscleGroup(String muscleGroup) { this.muscleGroup = muscleGroup; }
}

package com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.CascadeType;
import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.FetchType;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.JoinColumn;
import jakarta.persistence.ManyToOne;
import jakarta.persistence.OneToMany;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "exercise_entries")
public class ExerciseEntryEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Owning side of the session relationship — holds workout_session_id FK.
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "workout_session_id", nullable = false)
    private WorkoutSessionEntity workoutSession;

    // Reference to the exercise library — holds exercise_id FK.
    // Not ownership — the exercise exists independently of this entry.
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "exercise_id", nullable = false)
    private ExerciseEntity exercise;

    @Column(name = "order_index", nullable = false)
    private int orderIndex;

    // Inverse side — ExerciseEntryEntity does not own this FK.
    // CascadeType.ALL so sets persist and delete with the entry.
    // orphanRemoval so removing a set from the list deletes it from the DB.
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "exerciseEntry", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
    private List<SetEntryEntity> setEntries = new ArrayList<>();

    protected ExerciseEntryEntity() {}

    public ExerciseEntryEntity(ExerciseEntity exercise, int orderIndex) {
        this.exercise = exercise;
        this.orderIndex = orderIndex;
    }

    // Syncs both sides of the bidirectional relationship.
    // Always use this instead of manipulating the list directly.
    public void addSetEntry(SetEntryEntity setEntry) {
        setEntries.add(setEntry);
        setEntry.setExerciseEntry(this);
    }

    public void removeSetEntry(SetEntryEntity setEntry) {
        setEntries.remove(setEntry);
        setEntry.setExerciseEntry(null);
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public WorkoutSessionEntity getWorkoutSession() { return workoutSession; }
    public ExerciseEntity getExercise() { return exercise; }
    public int getOrderIndex() { return orderIndex; }

    // Unmodifiable so callers cannot bypass addSetEntry/removeSetEntry.
    public List<SetEntryEntity> getSetEntries() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(setEntries);
    }

    // Called by WorkoutSessionEntity.addExerciseEntry() to sync both sides.
    void setWorkoutSession(WorkoutSessionEntity workoutSession) {
        this.workoutSession = workoutSession;
    }

    public void setOrderIndex(int orderIndex) { this.orderIndex = orderIndex; }
}

package com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.FetchType;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.JoinColumn;
import jakarta.persistence.ManyToOne;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

@Entity
@Table(name = "set_entries")
public class SetEntryEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Owning side — this is where the FK column lives.
    // LAZY because we never need to load upward through the hierarchy.
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "exercise_entry_id", nullable = false)
    private ExerciseEntryEntity exerciseEntry;

    @Column(name = "set_number", nullable = false)
    private int setNumber;

    // Nullable — bodyweight exercises have no weight.
    @Column(precision = 6, scale = 2)
    private BigDecimal weight;

    // Nullable — timed sets don't use reps.
    private Integer reps;

    // Nullable — RPE is always optional.
    @Column(precision = 3, scale = 1)
    private BigDecimal rpe;

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private boolean completed = false;

    protected SetEntryEntity() {}

    public SetEntryEntity(int setNumber, BigDecimal weight, Integer reps, BigDecimal rpe) {
        this.setNumber = setNumber;
        this.weight = weight;
        this.reps = reps;
        this.rpe = rpe;
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public ExerciseEntryEntity getExerciseEntry() { return exerciseEntry; }
    public int getSetNumber() { return setNumber; }
    public BigDecimal getWeight() { return weight; }
    public Integer getReps() { return reps; }
    public BigDecimal getRpe() { return rpe; }
    public boolean isCompleted() { return completed; }

    // Called by ExerciseEntryEntity.addSetEntry() to sync both sides.
    void setExerciseEntry(ExerciseEntryEntity exerciseEntry) {
        this.exerciseEntry = exerciseEntry;
    }

    public void setWeight(BigDecimal weight) { this.weight = weight; }
    public void setReps(Integer reps) { this.reps = reps; }
    public void setRpe(BigDecimal rpe) { this.rpe = rpe; }
    public void setCompleted(boolean completed) { this.completed = completed; }
}

import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.FetchType;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.JoinColumn;
import jakarta.persistence.ManyToOne;
import jakarta.persistence.OneToMany;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "workout_plan_days")
public class WorkoutPlanDayEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Owning side — holds workout_plan_id FK.
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "workout_plan_id", nullable = false)
    private WorkoutPlanEntity workoutPlan;

    @Column(name = "day_label", nullable = false)
    private String dayLabel;

    @Column(name = "order_index", nullable = false)
    private int orderIndex;

    // Inverse side — cascades all operations down to exercises.
    // orphanRemoval deletes an exercise slot when removed from the list.
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "workoutPlanDay", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
    private List<PlanDayExerciseEntity> exercises = new ArrayList<>();

    protected WorkoutPlanDayEntity() {}

    public WorkoutPlanDayEntity(String dayLabel, int orderIndex) {
        this.dayLabel = dayLabel;
        this.orderIndex = orderIndex;
    }

    public void addExercise(PlanDayExerciseEntity exercise) {
        exercises.add(exercise);
        exercise.setWorkoutPlanDay(this);
    }

    public void removeExercise(PlanDayExerciseEntity exercise) {
        exercises.remove(exercise);
        exercise.setWorkoutPlanDay(null);
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public WorkoutPlanEntity getWorkoutPlan() { return workoutPlan; }
    public String getDayLabel() { return dayLabel; }
    public int getOrderIndex() { return orderIndex; }

    public List<PlanDayExerciseEntity> getExercises() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(exercises);
    }

    // Called by WorkoutPlanEntity.addDay() to sync both sides.
    void setWorkoutPlan(WorkoutPlanEntity workoutPlan) {
        this.workoutPlan = workoutPlan;
    }

    public void setDayLabel(String dayLabel) { this.dayLabel = dayLabel; }
    public void setOrderIndex(int orderIndex) { this.orderIndex = orderIndex; }
}

package com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.CascadeType;
import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.OneToMany;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "workout_plans")
public class WorkoutPlanEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Ownership anchor — Long by ID only, never a join to UserEntity.
    @Column(name = "owner_user_id", nullable = false)
    private Long ownerUserId;

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String name;

    @Column(name = "days_per_week", nullable = false)
    private int daysPerWeek;

    // PPL, Upper/Lower, Full Body, Custom — stored as String for flexibility.
    @Column(name = "split_type", nullable = false)
    private String splitType;

    // Only one plan active per user at a time. Enforced at service layer.
    @Column(name = "is_active", nullable = false)
    private boolean isActive = false;

    // Inverse side — full cascade means saving the plan saves all its days
    // and their exercises. Deleting the plan cascades all the way down.
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "workoutPlan", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
    private List<WorkoutPlanDayEntity> days = new ArrayList<>();

    protected WorkoutPlanEntity() {}

    public WorkoutPlanEntity(Long ownerUserId, String name, int daysPerWeek, String splitType) {
        this.ownerUserId = ownerUserId;
        this.name = name;
        this.daysPerWeek = daysPerWeek;
        this.splitType = splitType;
    }

    public void addDay(WorkoutPlanDayEntity day) {
        days.add(day);
        day.setWorkoutPlan(this);
    }

    public void removeDay(WorkoutPlanDayEntity day) {
        days.remove(day);
        day.setWorkoutPlan(null);
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public Long getOwnerUserId() { return ownerUserId; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public int getDaysPerWeek() { return daysPerWeek; }
    public String getSplitType() { return splitType; }
    public boolean isActive() { return isActive; }

    public List<WorkoutPlanDayEntity> getDays() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(days);
    }

    public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; }
    public void setDaysPerWeek(int daysPerWeek) { this.daysPerWeek = daysPerWeek; }
    public void setSplitType(String splitType) { this.splitType = splitType; }
    public void setActive(boolean active) { this.isActive = active; }
}

package com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.CascadeType;
import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.OneToMany;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;

@Entity
@Table(name = "workout_sessions")
public class WorkoutSessionEntity {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    // Ownership anchor — checked by the controller before any service call.
    // Long by ID only — the workouts domain never imports from identity.
    @Column(name = "owner_user_id", nullable = false)
    private Long ownerUserId;

    // Instant is timezone-safe. Always stored as UTC in MySQL DATETIME(6).
    @Column(name = "started_at", nullable = false)
    private Instant startedAt;

    // Null means session is still in progress.
    @Column(name = "finished_at")
    private Instant finishedAt;

    @Column(columnDefinition = "TEXT")
    private String notes;

    // Inverse side — WorkoutSessionEntity does not own the FK column.
    // CascadeType.ALL propagates persist, merge, remove down to entries.
    // orphanRemoval deletes an entry from the DB when removed from this list.
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "workoutSession", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
    private List<ExerciseEntryEntity> exerciseEntries = new ArrayList<>();

    protected WorkoutSessionEntity() {}

    public WorkoutSessionEntity(Long ownerUserId, Instant startedAt) {
        this.ownerUserId = ownerUserId;
        this.startedAt = startedAt;
    }

    // Always use these helpers — they sync both sides of the relationship.
    public void addExerciseEntry(ExerciseEntryEntity entry) {
        exerciseEntries.add(entry);
        entry.setWorkoutSession(this);
    }

    public void removeExerciseEntry(ExerciseEntryEntity entry) {
        exerciseEntries.remove(entry);
        entry.setWorkoutSession(null);
    }

    public Long getId() { return id; }
    public Long getOwnerUserId() { return ownerUserId; }
    public Instant getStartedAt() { return startedAt; }
    public Instant getFinishedAt() { return finishedAt; }
    public String getNotes() { return notes; }

    public List<ExerciseEntryEntity> getExerciseEntries() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(exerciseEntries);
    }

    public void setFinishedAt(Instant finishedAt) { this.finishedAt = finishedAt; }
    public void setNotes(String notes) { this.notes = notes; }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/workouts/service/ExerciseServiceImpl.java
================================================================================
package com.fitt.workouts.service;

import com.fitt.workouts.domain.MuscleGroup;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.CreateExerciseRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.ExerciseResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.ExerciseEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.ExerciseRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.ExerciseNotFoundException;
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.util.List;

@Service
@Transactional(readOnly = true)
public class ExerciseServiceImpl implements ExerciseService {

    private final ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository;

    public ExerciseServiceImpl(ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository) {
        this.exerciseRepository = exerciseRepository;
    }

    @Override
    public List<ExerciseResponse> listExercises(Long ownerUserId, MuscleGroup muscleGroup) {
        // pull fixed library + user's custom exercises, then optionally filter by muscle group
        List<ExerciseEntity> all = exerciseRepository.findByOwnerUserIdIsNullOrOwnerUserId(ownerUserId);

        return all.stream()
                .filter(e -> muscleGroup == null || e.getMuscleGroup().equals(muscleGroup.name()))
                .map(this::toResponse)
                .toList();
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public ExerciseResponse createCustomExercise(Long ownerUserId, CreateExerciseRequest request) {
        ExerciseEntity exercise = new ExerciseEntity();
        exercise.setName(request.name());
        exercise.setMuscleGroup(request.muscleGroup().name());
        exercise.setCustom(true);
        exercise.setOwnerUserId(ownerUserId);

        return toResponse(exerciseRepository.save(exercise));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public void deleteCustomExercise(Long ownerUserId, Long exerciseId) {
        ExerciseEntity exercise = exerciseRepository.findById(exerciseId)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ExerciseNotFoundException(exerciseId));

        if (!exercise.isCustom()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Fixed library exercises cannot be deleted");
        }

        if (!ownerUserId.equals(exercise.getOwnerUserId())) {
            throw new AccessDeniedException("You do not own this exercise");
        }

        exerciseRepository.delete(exercise);
    }

    private ExerciseResponse toResponse(ExerciseEntity entity) {
        return new ExerciseResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getName(),
                MuscleGroup.valueOf(entity.getMuscleGroup()),
                entity.isCustom()
        );
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/workouts/service/WorkoutPlanServiceImpl.java
================================================================================
package com.fitt.workouts.service;

import com.fitt.workouts.domain.SplitType;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.CreateWorkoutPlanDayRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.CreateWorkoutPlanRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.ExerciseResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.PlanDayExerciseResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.WorkoutPlanDayResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.WorkoutPlanResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.domain.MuscleGroup;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.ExerciseEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.PlanDayExerciseEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.WorkoutPlanDayEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.WorkoutPlanEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.ExerciseRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.WorkoutPlanRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.ExerciseNotFoundException;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.WorkoutPlanNotFoundException;
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

@Service
@Transactional(readOnly = true)
public class WorkoutPlanServiceImpl implements WorkoutPlanService {

    private final WorkoutPlanRepository planRepository;
    private final ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository;

    public WorkoutPlanServiceImpl(WorkoutPlanRepository planRepository,
                                  ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository) {
        this.planRepository = planRepository;
        this.exerciseRepository = exerciseRepository;
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutPlanResponse createPlan(Long ownerUserId, CreateWorkoutPlanRequest request) {
        WorkoutPlanEntity plan = new WorkoutPlanEntity();
        plan.setOwnerUserId(ownerUserId);
        plan.setName(request.name());
        plan.setDaysPerWeek(request.daysPerWeek());
        plan.setSplitType(request.splitType().name());
        plan.setActive(false);

        for (CreateWorkoutPlanDayRequest dayReq : request.days()) {
            WorkoutPlanDayEntity day = new WorkoutPlanDayEntity();
            day.setDayNumber(dayReq.dayNumber());
            day.setLabel(dayReq.label());

            if (dayReq.exerciseIds() != null) {
                int order = 0;
                for (Long exerciseId : dayReq.exerciseIds()) {
                    ExerciseEntity exercise = exerciseRepository.findById(exerciseId)
                            .orElseThrow(() -> new ExerciseNotFoundException(exerciseId));

                    PlanDayExerciseEntity slot = new PlanDayExerciseEntity();
                    slot.setOrderIndex(order++);
                    // day.addPlanDayExercise() syncs both sides
                    day.addPlanDayExercise(slot, exercise);
                }
            }

            // plan.addPlanDay() syncs both sides
            plan.addPlanDay(day);
        }

        return toResponse(planRepository.save(plan));
    }

    @Override
    public List<WorkoutPlanResponse> listPlans(Long ownerUserId) {
        return planRepository.findByOwnerUserIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(ownerUserId)
                .stream()
                .map(this::toResponse)
                .toList();
    }

    @Override
    public WorkoutPlanResponse getPlan(Long ownerUserId, Long planId) {
        return toResponse(loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, planId));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutPlanResponse activatePlan(Long ownerUserId, Long planId) {
        // deactivate all first, then activate the one we want
        List<WorkoutPlanEntity> allPlans = planRepository.findByOwnerUserId(ownerUserId);
        allPlans.forEach(p -> p.setActive(false));
        planRepository.saveAll(allPlans);

        WorkoutPlanEntity target = allPlans.stream()
                .filter(p -> p.getId().equals(planId))
                .findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new WorkoutPlanNotFoundException(planId));

        target.setActive(true);

        return toResponse(planRepository.save(target));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public void deletePlan(Long ownerUserId, Long planId) {
        WorkoutPlanEntity plan = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, planId);
        planRepository.delete(plan);
    }

    private WorkoutPlanEntity loadAndVerifyOwnership(Long ownerUserId, Long planId) {
        WorkoutPlanEntity plan = planRepository.findById(planId)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new WorkoutPlanNotFoundException(planId));

        if (!ownerUserId.equals(plan.getOwnerUserId())) {
            throw new AccessDeniedException("You do not own this plan");
        }

        return plan;
    }

    private WorkoutPlanResponse toResponse(WorkoutPlanEntity entity) {
        List<WorkoutPlanDayResponse> days = entity.getPlanDays()
                .stream()
                .map(this::toDayResponse)
                .toList();

        return new WorkoutPlanResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getOwnerUserId(),
                entity.getName(),
                entity.getDaysPerWeek(),
                SplitType.valueOf(entity.getSplitType()),
                entity.isActive(),
                entity.getCreatedAt(),
                days
        );
    }

    private WorkoutPlanDayResponse toDayResponse(WorkoutPlanDayEntity entity) {
        List<PlanDayExerciseResponse> exercises = entity.getPlanDayExercises()
                .stream()
                .map(this::toPlanDayExerciseResponse)
                .toList();

        return new WorkoutPlanDayResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getDayNumber(),
                entity.getLabel(),
                exercises
        );
    }

    private PlanDayExerciseResponse toPlanDayExerciseResponse(PlanDayExerciseEntity entity) {
        ExerciseResponse exercise = new ExerciseResponse(
                entity.getExercise().getId(),
                entity.getExercise().getName(),
                MuscleGroup.valueOf(entity.getExercise().getMuscleGroup()),
                entity.getExercise().isCustom()
        );

        return new PlanDayExerciseResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getOrderIndex(),
                exercise
        );
    }
}

FILE: backend/src/main/java/com/fitt/workouts/service/WorkoutSessionServiceImpl.java

package com.fitt.workouts.service;

import com.fitt.workouts.domain.MuscleGroup;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.AddExerciseEntryRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.CreateWorkoutSessionRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.ExerciseEntryResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.ExerciseResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.LogSetRequest;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.SetEntryResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.dto.WorkoutSessionResponse;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.ExerciseEntryEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.ExerciseEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.SetEntryEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.persistence.entity.WorkoutSessionEntity;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.ExerciseEntryRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.ExerciseRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.SetEntryRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.repository.WorkoutSessionRepository;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.ExerciseNotFoundException;
import com.fitt.workouts.service.exception.WorkoutSessionNotFoundException;
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;

@Service
@Transactional(readOnly = true)
public class WorkoutSessionServiceImpl implements WorkoutSessionService {

    private final WorkoutSessionRepository sessionRepository;
    private final ExerciseEntryRepository entryRepository;
    private final SetEntryRepository setEntryRepository;
    private final ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository;

    public WorkoutSessionServiceImpl(
            WorkoutSessionRepository sessionRepository,
            ExerciseEntryRepository entryRepository,
            SetEntryRepository setEntryRepository,
            ExerciseRepository exerciseRepository) {
        this.sessionRepository = sessionRepository;
        this.entryRepository = entryRepository;
        this.setEntryRepository = setEntryRepository;
        this.exerciseRepository = exerciseRepository;
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse createSession(Long ownerUserId, CreateWorkoutSessionRequest request) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = new WorkoutSessionEntity();
        session.setOwnerUserId(ownerUserId);
        session.setStartedAt(request.startedAt());
        session.setWorkoutPlanDayId(request.workoutPlanDayId());
        session.setNotes(request.notes());

        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    @Override
    public List<WorkoutSessionResponse> listSessions(Long ownerUserId) {
        return sessionRepository.findByOwnerUserIdOrderByStartedAtDesc(ownerUserId)
                .stream()
                .map(this::toResponse)
                .toList();
    }

    @Override
    public WorkoutSessionResponse getSession(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);
        return toResponse(session);
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse finishSession(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);
        session.setFinishedAt(Instant.now());
        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public void deleteSession(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);
        sessionRepository.delete(session);
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse addExerciseEntry(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId, AddExerciseEntryRequest request) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);

        ExerciseEntity exercise = exerciseRepository.findById(request.exerciseId())
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ExerciseNotFoundException(request.exerciseId()));

        // append to the end of whatever is already in this session
        int nextIndex = session.getExerciseEntries().size();

        ExerciseEntryEntity entry = new ExerciseEntryEntity();
        entry.setOrderIndex(nextIndex);
        // session.addExerciseEntry() keeps both sides of the relationship in sync
        session.addExerciseEntry(entry, exercise);

        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse removeExerciseEntry(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId, Long entryId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);

        ExerciseEntryEntity target = session.getExerciseEntries()
                .stream()
                .filter(e -> e.getId().equals(entryId))
                .findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Exercise entry not found in this session"));

        // orphanRemoval on the parent takes care of the DELETE
        session.removeExerciseEntry(target);

        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse logSet(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId, Long entryId, LogSetRequest request) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);

        ExerciseEntryEntity entry = session.getExerciseEntries()
                .stream()
                .filter(e -> e.getId().equals(entryId))
                .findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Exercise entry not found in this session"));

        int nextSetNumber = entry.getSetEntries().size() + 1;

        SetEntryEntity set = new SetEntryEntity();
        set.setSetNumber(nextSetNumber);
        set.setReps(request.reps());
        set.setWeightKg(request.weightKg());
        set.setRpe(request.rpe());
        set.setCompletedAt(Instant.now());
        // entry.addSetEntry() syncs both sides
        entry.addSetEntry(set);

        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional
    public WorkoutSessionResponse deleteSet(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId, Long entryId, Long setId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = loadAndVerifyOwnership(ownerUserId, sessionId);

        ExerciseEntryEntity entry = session.getExerciseEntries()
                .stream()
                .filter(e -> e.getId().equals(entryId))
                .findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Exercise entry not found in this session"));

        SetEntryEntity target = entry.getSetEntries()
                .stream()
                .filter(s -> s.getId().equals(setId))
                .findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Set not found in this exercise entry"));

        entry.removeSetEntry(target);

        return toResponse(sessionRepository.save(session));
    }

    // load and verify ownership in one shot
    // every operation goes through this before doing anything
    private WorkoutSessionEntity loadAndVerifyOwnership(Long ownerUserId, Long sessionId) {
        WorkoutSessionEntity session = sessionRepository.findById(sessionId)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new WorkoutSessionNotFoundException(sessionId));

        if (!ownerUserId.equals(session.getOwnerUserId())) {
            throw new AccessDeniedException("You do not own this session");
        }

        return session;
    }

    private WorkoutSessionResponse toResponse(WorkoutSessionEntity entity) {
        List<ExerciseEntryResponse> entries = entity.getExerciseEntries()
                .stream()
                .map(this::toEntryResponse)
                .toList();

        return new WorkoutSessionResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getOwnerUserId(),
                entity.getWorkoutPlanDayId(),
                entity.getStartedAt(),
                entity.getFinishedAt(),
                entity.getNotes(),
                entity.getCreatedAt(),
                entries
        );
    }

    private ExerciseEntryResponse toEntryResponse(ExerciseEntryEntity entity) {
        List<SetEntryResponse> sets = entity.getSetEntries()
                .stream()
                .map(this::toSetResponse)
                .toList();

        ExerciseResponse exercise = new ExerciseResponse(
                entity.getExercise().getId(),
                entity.getExercise().getName(),
                MuscleGroup.valueOf(entity.getExercise().getMuscleGroup()),
                entity.getExercise().isCustom()
        );

        return new ExerciseEntryResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getOrderIndex(),
                exercise,
                sets
        );
    }

    private SetEntryResponse toSetResponse(SetEntryEntity entity) {
        return new SetEntryResponse(
                entity.getId(),
                entity.getSetNumber(),
                entity.getReps(),
                entity.getWeightKg(),
                entity.getRpe(),
                entity.getCompletedAt()
        );
    }
}

# Getting Started

* [Create an OCI image](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.0.1/maven-plugin/build-image.html)
* [Spring Data JPA](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.0.1/reference/data/sql.html#data.sql.jpa-and-spring-data)
* [Spring Security](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.0.1/reference/web/spring-security.html)
* [Validation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.0.1/reference/io/validation.html)
* [Spring Web](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.0.1/reference/web/servlet.html)

### Guides

The following guides illustrate how to use some features concretely:

* [Accessing Data with JPA](https://spring.io/guides/gs/accessing-data-jpa/)
* [Securing a Web Application](https://spring.io/guides/gs/securing-web/)
* [Spring Boot and OAuth2](https://spring.io/guides/tutorials/spring-boot-oauth2/)
* [Authenticating a User with LDAP](https://spring.io/guides/gs/authenticating-ldap/)
* [Validation](https://spring.io/guides/gs/validating-form-input/)
* [Building a RESTful Web Service](https://spring.io/guides/gs/rest-service/)
* [Serving Web Content with Spring MVC](https://spring.io/guides/gs/serving-web-content/)
* [Building REST services with Spring](https://spring.io/guides/tutorials/rest/)

### Maven Parent overrides

Due to Maven's design, elements are inherited from the parent POM to the project POM.
While most of the inheritance is fine, it also inherits unwanted elements like `<license>` and `<developers>` from the
parent.
To prevent this, the project POM contains empty overrides for these elements.
If you manually switch to a different parent and actually want the inheritance, you need to remove those overrides.

# ADR-0001: Architecture Style for FITT

Status: Accepted  
Date: 2025-12-23

## Decision

For version 1, FITT will use a modular monolith architecture for the backend, with a separate frontend client consuming a single backend API.

The backend will be deployed as one application, but structured internally into clear modules with well-defined responsibilities and boundaries. These modules will communicate through explicit interfaces rather than shared, unrestricted access.

## Context

This project is both a learning effort and a real application I intend to use. I am working as a solo developer with limited time, budget, and infrastructure. Early complexity must be controlled while still allowing the system to grow in a clean and professional way.

The application will support a web frontend initially (Angular), with a long-term goal of adding an iOS client. Both clients should be able to rely on the same backend API without changes to business logic.

## Rationale

A modular monolith fits these constraints because it:

- Keeps deployment simple (one backend service)
- Avoids the operational and cognitive overhead of microservices
- Encourages clean separation of concerns inside the backend
- Makes future refactoring or extraction of modules possible if needed
- Is widely recommended as a starting point for systems that may grow

Separating the frontend and backend allows independent development and supports multiple client types while keeping the backend authoritative for business rules and data integrity.

## Alternatives Considered

Microservices were considered but rejected for v1 due to:
- Increased operational complexity
- Infrastructure overhead
- Higher risk of premature abstraction
- Poor fit for a solo developer at this stage

A fully monolithic backend without internal modular boundaries was also rejected, as it would make the system harder to reason about and evolve over time.

## Consequences

This decision means:
- The backend will enforce boundaries through package structure and design
- Architectural discipline is required to prevent cross-module coupling
- Scaling will focus on code organization and clarity, not service proliferation
- Future extraction into separate services remains possible but is not required

This architecture supports learning, maintainability, and future growth without unnecessary complexity.

# ADR-0002: Backend Domain Modules for FITT

Status: Accepted  
Date: 2025-12-23

## Decision

For version 1, the FITT backend will be structured as a modular monolith with the following core domain modules:

- Identity
- Workouts
- Measurements
- Nutrition

Each module owns its data, rules, and persistence. Modules communicate through explicit service boundaries rather than shared, unrestricted access.

## Context

FITT is a web-first, API-first application intended to support future clients such as iOS. The backend must remain clean, understandable, and extensible while being feasible for a solo developer.

Early design decisions should avoid overly narrow domains that block future growth, while still keeping v1 focused and simple.

## Module Definitions

### Identity

Owns:
- User accounts
- Authentication and authorization
- Profile-related data (non-fitness)

Does not own:
- Fitness metrics
- Workouts
- Nutrition logic

### Workouts

Owns:
- Workout programs and routines
- Exercise selections
- Set, rep, and scheme definitions
- Progressive overload structure

Does not own:
- User identity
- Body measurements
- Nutrition calculations

### Measurements

Owns:
- Weight logs (v1)
- Historical measurement tracking
- Time-based measurement history

Future extensions may include:
- Body fat percentage
- Circumference measurements
- Performance metrics such as RPE

Does not own:
- Workout definitions
- Nutrition logic

### Nutrition

Owns:
- Calorie targets and recommendations
- Goal-based calorie logic (cut, maintain, bulk)

Does not own:
- Food databases
- Barcode scanning
- Meal-level tracking

## Dependency Rules

- Identity has no dependency on other modules
- Workouts may depend on Identity for user ownership
- Measurements may depend on Identity for user ownership
- Nutrition may depend on Identity and Measurements
- No module may directly access another module’s persistence layer

## Consequences

This structure:
- Keeps responsibilities clear
- Allows future expansion without breaking v1
- Prevents god services and cross-module coupling
- Supports long-term bodybuilding and powerlifting features such as RPE without forcing them into v1

The tradeoff is that discipline is required to maintain boundaries as the codebase grows.

# ADR-0003: V1 Domain Models Approved

Status: Accepted  
Date: 2025-12-24

## Decision

I have completed and approved the v1 domain model diagrams for FITT. These diagrams define the core entities, attributes, and relationships for version 1 across the four domains:

- Identity
- Workouts
- Measurements
- Nutrition

These diagrams will be treated as the source of truth for initial entity design and will guide implementation of JPA entities, DTOs, and REST endpoints.

## Scope

The diagrams capture domain concepts and relationships, not database schema or UI design.

The diagrams intentionally exclude:
- Food database and barcode scanning
- Social features
- Medical or nutritional coaching liability
- Advanced powerlifting/bodybuilding features beyond initial RPE placement

## Artifacts

The following artifacts are approved and stored under docs/architecture:

- domain-identity
- domain-workouts
- domain-measurements
- domain-nutrition

## Consequences

Implementation should follow these domain models unless I explicitly revise them via a new ADR.

If future features require structural changes, I will update the diagrams and create an ADR documenting the change before modifying core entities.

# Phase 5: Workouts API Contract v1

This file is the contract for the Workouts endpoints. Controllers must match this behavior exactly so the frontend can integrate without guessing. Internals can evolve later, but this contract stays stable unless I explicitly version it.

## Auth and ownership rules

- All `/api/workouts/**` endpoints require authentication.
- Ownership-safe behavior is mandatory:
- If a workout does not exist OR it exists but belongs to a different user, return `404 Not Found`.
- Do not return `403` for “not owned” because that confirms the resource exists.

## Content types

- Requests: `Content-Type: application/json`
- Responses: `Content-Type: application/json` (except 204)

## Public DTOs

CreateWorkoutRequest
- `name` string, required, must not be blank

WorkoutResponse
- `id` integer
- `name` string
- `createdAt` ISO-8601 timestamp string
- `updatedAt` ISO-8601 timestamp string

Error format (Problem Details, RFC 9457 style)
- We return one consistent error shape everywhere.
- Fields:
- `type` string (URI), optional but preferred
- `title` string
- `status` integer
- `detail` string
- `instance` string (URI), optional

## Endpoints

### POST /api/workouts

What it does
- Creates a workout owned by the authenticated user.

Request body
- CreateWorkoutRequest

Example body
- `{ "name": "Push Day" }`

Success
- `201 Created`
- Response body is the created WorkoutResponse

Validation errors
- `400 Bad Request`
- Problem Details payload (example cases: missing name, blank name)

### GET /api/workouts/{workoutId}

What it does
- Returns one workout by id, but only if it belongs to the authenticated user.

Path param
- `workoutId` integer, required

Success
- `200 OK`
- WorkoutResponse

Not found / not owned
- `404 Not Found` (ownership-safe)

### DELETE /api/workouts/{workoutId}

What it does
- Deletes one workout by id, but only if it belongs to the authenticated user.

Path param
- `workoutId` integer, required

Success
- `204 No Content`
- No response body

Not found / not owned
- `404 Not Found` (ownership-safe)

## Implementation notes (non-negotiable)

- Controllers do not return entities directly.
- Controllers map request DTO -> service call -> response DTO.
- Errors are uniform Problem Details (no random `{ "error": "..." }` shapes).

# FITT Architecture (C4)

We will use two C4 diagrams to describe FITT at the start:
- System Context
- Container

C4 is a lightweight way to describe software architecture using a consistent set of diagram types and abstractions.

## System Context, what exists

Purpose
Show the system boundary. Who uses FITT and what external systems it depends on.

Actors
- End user (lifter)

Software systems
- FITT (the system)
- Database (local in development, hosted in production later)

Future systems (not v1)
- Messaging or sharing services
- Cloud hosting and remote sync
- iOS client using the same backend API

Draw.io instructions
Create a diagram with two boxes and one person:
- Person: End user
- Box: FITT
Connect End user -> FITT with “uses”

Optionally annotate that FITT stores data in a database, but keep it high level.

## Container view (how it runs)

Purpose
Show the runtime pieces that make FITT work and how they communicate.

Containers
- Web client (browser UI)
- Backend API (rules, auth, persistence orchestration)
- Database (source of truth for user data)

Trust boundaries
- Browser client is untrusted
- API is the enforcement boundary
- Database is private to the API

Draw.io instructions
Create three boxes and one person:
- Person: End user
- Box: Web client
- Box: Backend API
- Cylinder: Database

Connections
- End user -> Web client “uses”
- Web client -> Backend API “HTTPS/JSON”
- Backend API -> Database “SQL”

Diagram checklist
Before you consider the diagram done, verify that:
- Every box has a clear responsibility
- The database is not connected directly to the user
- The API is the boundary where validation and authorization live

# FITT — Sprint 0 Blueprint
Status: Approved
Last updated: 2025-12-23

This document explains why FITT exists, who it is for, what success means, what is out of scope for v1, and when the project should stop. It is the foundation for the architecture and repo setup that comes next.

## Why this project exists

There is a gap in the fitness app space for people who lift weights and want a simple, budget-friendly tool that supports real training progress. Many apps are expensive, noisy, or bloated. Users end up tracking in journals, guessing calories, or relying on memory. That makes training harder than it needs to be and can slow progress.

This project exists because that pain shows up daily for lifters, and the founder is also a user with the same problem.

## Who this is for

Primary user
A person who trains with intention. This includes bodybuilders, powerlifters, and anyone serious about tracking workouts and progress.

Not the user
People who do not care about training, diet, or tracking progress.

Context and constraints
The problem appears when the user forgets what they did last session, cannot track progressive overload cleanly, or feels unsure about calories and goals. Common constraints are attention, memory, consistency, and knowledge.

## What success looks like

If FITT succeeds, the user feels confident that their training and diet choices are reasonable. It becomes easier to answer questions like surplus vs deficit and how progressive overload applies in practice.

Success is measurable
Strength increases over time, weight trends move in the intended direction, and physique improves. The user can look back and see proof of progress.

## What v1 will not do

v1 is intentionally limited. It will not include:
- A MyFitnessPal-style food database or barcode scanning
- Social features like friends, sharing, feeds, or messaging
- Medical advice, clinical nutrition guidance, or coaching liability

These boundaries exist to prevent a half-built product and to avoid security and quality shortcuts.

## Project shape and constraints

This is both a learning project and a real tool I intend to use. If it proves useful, it may become portfolio-ready and later public or commercial.

Current constraints include time, money, and developing full-stack and mobile skills. Infrastructure should remain simple.

Reliability expectation for v1
Hobby-grade is acceptable, but the system must persist data. Workout history should not be casually lost. A real database is required, even if it is local in early stages.

Platform direction
Long term, the goal is iOS. v1 will be web-first to maximize learning and interview readiness, while keeping the API reusable for a future iOS client.

## Data and responsibility

Data handled includes:
- Name, date of birth, age, email, password
- Optional phone for 2FA, locale
- Fitness metrics, goals, workout history

Most sensitive data
Passwords and identifiers. Payment information would be highly sensitive if added later.

Accuracy expectations
Age, height, goals, and calories must be accurate for recommendations to be meaningful. Some estimates (like daily calorie expenditure) can be approximate.

Responsibility model
The system provides suggestions and structure. The user is responsible for applying it safely and consistently.

## Trust, ethics, and limits

Risks
Users may over-trust the system or assume results are automatic without discipline.

Boundaries
The app must present recommendations as suggestions and avoid claiming medical or nutritional authority. It is not a doctor, nutritionist, or personal coach.

## Stop conditions

Stop or pause if:
- Users are consistently unhappy, stability is poor, or reviews are overwhelmingly negative
- A security breach occurs that undermines trust
- The project does not reach a minimally functional state

It is irresponsible to charge users if promises are not met or if the product is unreliable.

## Deferred vision (not v1)

Future capabilities that are explicitly deferred:
- Barcode scanning and food databases
- Exercise demonstration media
- Onboarding maintenance-calorie estimation and recalculation flows
- Custom templates, default workouts, and recommended weights/sets/reps
- RPE and advanced bodybuilding/powerlifting tracking needs
- Social features

These are recorded to preserve the vision without letting v1 collapse under scope.
